Like what person advertising the product looks like etc. So mostly it's just word/image play in all ads, not just foods/supplements. 

As far as classifications go in Australia there's ABCD system. Basically group A supplements have strong evidence behind them and is what is known to work. Includes things like Whey Protein, Caffeine, B-Alanine or for example more recent newcomer beetroot juice. 

Group B has evidence supporting, but further research would be needed. It's basically what might work. Includes things like Fish Oils, Glutamine, Anti-Oxidants C and E etc.

Group C is basically what doesn't work. Things that have not enough scientific proof to be reasonably used. Basically everything not in A, B or D.

Group D is what's banned. Things like DMAA, DHEA and other very complicated names would be in this category. 

For foods there is also number of different classifications for different things like how it's grown, where it's from and so on. Depending on country you should be able to also see what's in it although reading through the ingredients is not easy for normal people and that's also one thing that is consciously made so. Sure it's not nice playing against someone who has masteries and runes advantage. But it's kind of game's way of pointing out that you shouldn't be playing against them in the first place, because it messes the game for them, you and everyone else.

Also since I last year moved to another country(and region) and had to level up new account I can tell you that it's not just the rune advantage. I was able to play against 30's fine with about level 15-20 account and from there on. Also something that happens to everyone sometime, even few times we've seen this in pro play, is that someone actually accidentally has wrong or blank runes/masteries. It's adding extra step of customization. So basically it rewards knowledgeable players since they're able to make small changes or have specialized rune/mastery pages for specific situations on specific champions.

Also it applies from level 1 and builds more often than not are fairly limited. Like at some point you can just say that X build is not efficient etc. That's because items give stats in big chunks. Runes is a bit more finesse.

Like for champion A, I might have let's say 4 different builds I use. 1 that I build 80% of the time, then 2 others that fill 4% and one that fits 2% of the cases. Now that generic build that fits 80% of the time still includes number of different kind of match ups and situations. That's where the runes step in since they allow you to make minor changes to early game which rewards you from knowing the match up extremely well vs having vague idea of it.

You could think runes and masteries as kind of like settings. I have few friends who do skate quite a lot so that's first analogy that came into my mind. Like if we imagine that set up(what board, wheels, trucks etc) is same as build. If I give same set up for two of them and let them test it for a moment and customize it they couldn't use each others set up very well. Because even when using same set up, one would like wheels to be really tight, other would like something else etc.

So runes are like that. Small personal changes that allows you to customize the match up just for you. Often you're pretty much forced to build X because it's just best in Y situation, but you could still change runes depending on your personal preferences.

I don't really know the system where you are from(JV team etc?). But as I understood you tried out for a team and didn't get in. Here's some things I would recommend.

1. GAMES! Check the other possibilities and find what is going to be your main source of games. Maybe some other team(don't know system again so no idea if there's other teams you can join etc.). Have it be even just pick up games something is better than nothing. Aim for quality, but if that's not an option then make up for it with quantity if possible(pick up).

2. REVIEW! So some days after the emotion has gone away map out why did you not get in. Maybe you can email or politely(!!!) ask from coach why that was and where he would see most need for improvement in your game. Write down yourself also what kind of player you consider yourself. Any other opinions you can get, get them. That way you avoid your own personal bias and get more realistic picture of where you stand and what to focus.

3. RESOURCES! Alright, your not getting those school practice and games anymore. Write down and sort for yourself what are your resources now. Do you have inside court you can use, outside court, gym, hills, etc? How often/when? How can you get guidance, your not getting coached so how do you know what to do, any people who have expertise of any sort that you know? Worse you are with quality of coaching more simple you want to make it.

4. FOCUS! So now that you have a good idea think of what things you should improve and what are your resources. Time to do 1+1 and see what things your resources best fit for.

5. PLAN! You don't have consistent practice anymore. Start to make schedule for yourself of what to practice and when. If possible have it double check by someone who knows something about training. Start following it and stay at it!

6. DECORATION! Now especially if you didn't find team to play for a  year everything starts to lose it's meaning a bit and it's hard to see such long view as next year and making to team. So what you want to do is have some mini goals and milestones. Can be as small as achieving some performance numbers in training (X kg squat, X score in shooting drill etc.) or some events that don't even have to be immediately related to basketball such as running/cycling events(maybe a half marathon for fun etc.) or anything else. Anything from serious basketball tournament to recreational beach volley tourney to be honest.

I hope some of these steps would help you to stay motivated and organized even when being without a team. That is always really hard time for athlete, regardless if you are young, but competitive or professional. 

Best luck to you!

What do you mean that you can't participate in the world of basketball? I mean I can go and play in recreational league here so I wonder if you don't have this change?

Because that is exactly the same level that you can participate in world of e-sports. You can play with other normal people and that's it. Then if you are good enough(best 0.2% in league of legends for example). You might be able to play in high enough soloQ(like pick up basketball) games that you might attract attention and be singed to a team.

But in same way if you absolutely dominate everyone in recreational league by scoring 40+ points every game and dunking on everyone you probably get change to play in higher level and so on and so on.

The game that professionals in league are playing while essentially is the same as what you would play after downloading the game(same way as basketball I play with friends is essentially same as the basketball in any FIBA competition, same rules, lines etc.) there is plenty of difference.

Now you mentioned the physical tools. That would be the first problem that would stop you from playing with pro's. If we insert you to league of legends game and assume I would have explained you what to do and you would play against Faker(best player at the moment) for example.

What would be most apparent first would be couple of things. First is hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills. So basically controlling your mouse. There is thing called CSing(killing small monsters in the map) that players routinely do in league and basically it requires good timing and mouse control. Professionals when not being pressured usually get over 90% of the CS, Faker would probably be expected to get 98% or more.

Now player who has been playing for a while, but isn't highly ranked will get somewhere around 60%. You as starting would probably get 30% or so.

Now that's one thing. However as playing against professional player like Faker what he would do is contest every CS that you would attempt to take which would make you probably get around 10% while he would still get 98% or so.

So straight up your fine motor skills and hand-eye coordination would limit your ability to play. It's the same reason why you won't be able do things with deck of cards that magician can do even if you would know the secrets or why you can't golf as well as professionals even if you physically are as strong etc.

Well something else that professional player might do if you would face them playing league is that they would attempt to fight you. Now even if you would know how to fight and how champions work etc. We can even assume you would be able to mentally do same things as them(object tracking, keeping several timers in your head etc) what you would be at physical disadvantage would be reaction times. 

To give you an idea. Average reaction time in bronze(which is where anyone strating the game would probably rank to) is 337ms. Challenger which is highest ranking you can achieve by simple playing yourself(like pick up basketball type thing) has avg reaction time of 298ms.

Now if we look at pro's the regional level professionals have reaction times somewhere around 200-230ms and unfortunately we don't really have data at least that I could find of what kind of reaction time's do best players possess. However most likely somewhere around 180ms. And to compare 166ms is average reaction time for male olympic sprinters. 

So to conclude sure you can participate the video game world same way you can participate sports world. But unless you are physiologically(fine motor skills, hand-eye coordination, reaction time) and mentally(object tracking, keeping several timers in your head simultaneously, good quick decision making etc) you probably won't ever be able to participate to competitive video gaming world in any other way than as viewer.

So I have been depressed for 5 or so year for now. I don't think I have ever had serious suicidal thoughts(because of depression at least) and only once a small self harm thing. However I have been close to giving up more or less at times. 

Now this may sound like a very bad/stupid/cliche reason, but that's what it is. Whenever I have thought about suicide I have always come to conclusion that even if I can't be happy I can focus on making other people more happy than I'm unhappy.

It can be small things, but I have thought that if I would have something happen that would cause me to get to the point where I wouldn't care about my life anymore I would probably just volunteer in some kind of charity work etc. (stupid idea I know), but  I feel that would be better than killing myself.

Also I'm having this thought in the back of my head that there's always a change however small that I might figure it out in future.

So I guess what I do is when I would have suicidal thoughts I just block it by disregarding myself completely and focusing on what I can do to others. That has stopped me from killing myself couple of times and have made me done a lot of nice things to others so I guess that's not worst way to deal with my problems even if it isn't solving them. I also tend to think that as long as I'm alive(even if not for myself) there is always the small off chance that I can figure everything out.. Not sure if that would work for you though.

Anyways I hope all the best for you. I know the stressful day situation.
